physical: Warming a body by a given amount takes more heat the larger its heat capacity: thermal inertia. Q = C × ΔT
reflected_sentence: Read as thermal inertia, the cost turns around: what grew harder as the unnamed holding-in of warmth grew, now eases as receptivity rises; read as a plain ratio, the relation simply keeps its shape.
rule_reason: There is one cost and it rises with heat capacity, which the fixed list leaves UNDETERMINED: as thermal inertia it carries resistance and the single cost turns the relation; as a plain ratio it carries nothing and the relation keeps. closing: This is the one row the rule could not decide on its own: the fixed list explicitly punts on heat capacity, and the two readings give opposite shapes. I chose turns around to match this entry's stated cost reading, and confidence is correspondingly low.
